reason: This text from 1 Samuel 18-20 is a narrative focused on the covenant relationship between David and Jonathan and Saul's jealous pursuit of David. While Yahweh is invoked multiple times in oaths and covenants (e.g., 'Yahweh, God of Israel' in Jonathan's oath, and 'Yahweh will be between me and you forever'), the text contains no statement or implication that Yahweh doesn't owe loyalty to His people or that He considers replacing them with another people. The theological position described in the statement—divine rejection of the people and consideration of replacement—is not present in this passage. The text emphasizes covenantal loyalty and Yahweh's presence with David, not divine abandonment or replacement of the people.
